_doc: A concept's target sheet for the saloon (#765, #660; docs/briefs/saloon-design.md). The views are painted on GitHub (tools/buildings/target_sheet.py, building_sheet.yml); `plans` is drawn by tools/buildings/concept_plans.py from ../concept.json and given to the painted views. A target, not a blueprint: the spec settles every size. Painted 2026-11-10 at Sean's $5 pre-approval ($1.25 a concept). Second run (B only, Sean's pick, 2026-11-10): the open well over the card tables added (Sean: "an open view from the second floor to the main floor so people can fall over the rail"); the cutaway and the door view repainted and the gallery view added; cap raised to $1.55 (the four concepts' total stays under $5).
sheet_title: Salt Creek, 1882: The Salt Creek saloon, concept B, the corner saloon (target sheet, #765/#660)
look: Realistic concept art for a AAA open-world Western game set in 1882, in the direction of Red Dead Redemption 2's art book: photographic realism, natural light, real worn materials (sawn and planed pine, paint, glass, iron, brick, brass, dust), period-accurate in every object. No modern objects. No text other than the signs named. No border, no frame, no watermark, no captions.
building: THE SALT CREEK, a corner saloon built in 1881 by a man who meant to stay: a two-storey wood-frame building filling the corner, 54 ft along Main Street and 72 ft along the North-South Street, with a low hipped roof behind a level parapet and a bracketed wooden cornice on both street faces, painted dark red with cream trim. Its south-west corner is cut off on the diagonal at the ground floor (an 8 ft corner entrance with glazed double doors and a transom facing the crossroads), the upper floor carried over it on a single turned cast-iron column at the corner. Tall plate-glass windows along both streets, with 'THE SALT CREEK' in gilt letters on the glass and a long signboard over the corner. The balcony wraps the corner: along the whole Main Street front and down the North-South Street side for 44 ft, on posts at the edge of the boardwalks of both streets (a boardwalk runs down the side street too), with doors onto it from the dance hall and the owner's corner office. The outside stair is on the east side, in the saloon's yard: an open timber stair with a landing to a door on the upper floor's hall, seen from Main Street across the yard. Ground floor: one big bar room 54 x 44 ft, entered at the corner, the bar along the east wall straight ahead to the right, six posts in two rows carrying two girders; behind it, through a wide arch, the gaming room (faro, a wheel, poker), a stair hall with its own side door on the North-South Street and the stair up, a kitchen and lunch counter, a store room with the trapdoor to the cellar and the back door to the yard. Upstairs: the dance hall 36 x 44 ft over the bar's half of the bar room, its floor closed over the bar (fiddler's platform in its far corner); beside it, over the card tables on the west side of the bar room, an OPEN WELL 14 x 22 ft through the second floor with a turned wooden railing round it and a narrow gallery along the west wall, so from the dance hall's open west side and the gallery you look straight down 13 ft onto the card tables and the bar room, and the bar room's drinkers look up at the dancers over the rail; the owner's office in the corner over the entrance with windows on both streets, rented rooms behind. Based on the corner saloons at Tombstone, the Oriental and the Crystal Palace (1880-82), and Piper's Old Corner Bar at Virginia City, Nevada, a two-storey corner building with the bar below and rooms above. It stands in Salt Creek, a two-year-old Colorado mining-and-ranching boom town in the foothills, in 1882, on the north-east corner of the town's one crossroads: its front faces south onto Main Street (a wide dirt street, 66 ft between the building fronts), its west side faces the North-South Street, and on its east side is its own fenced yard, 34 ft wide, with a wagon gate; behind it, at the back of the 125 ft lot, a back street. The ground rises gently toward the back. A raised plank boardwalk 8 ft deep runs along Main Street in front, its top about 3 ft above the dirt, with steps down at the door and at the corner, and a hitching rail at its edge. Second floor: a dance hall over the bar room (its floor framed with joists on a timber girder carried by posts that stand in the bar room below; the bar room has no ceiling, so the joists and the underside of the floorboards are seen from below), and rented rooms and the owner's office. A wooden balcony over the boardwalk at the second floor, carried on plain square timber posts standing at the boardwalk's street edge, with a wooden railing and balusters; doors from upstairs open onto it. A timber outside stair runs up the building's side to a door on the upper floor. A cellar for kegs and barrels. Inside the bar room: a long bar of dark varnished wood about 42 in high with a brass foot rail and spittoons along it; behind it a tall back bar with a big mirror in panels, shelves of bottles and glasses; kerosene hanging lamps and wall brackets; a wide-plank pine floor, worn and scattered with sawdust; a big cast-iron stove with its pipe; round card tables with bentwood and plank chairs; a faro table; an upright piano; framed prints, a mounted elk head, a calendar and painted notices on board or papered walls. Front doors are glazed double doors with a transom (no swinging batwing doors).

views.title: Front (south), from Main Street
views.view: The whole front of the building seen straight on from the middle of Main Street at eye level, at golden hour (the low sun shining down the street from the west, raking across the front from the left), the whole front up to its cornice, the balcony and every one of its posts, the boardwalk, its steps and hitching rail in frame, a bit of the North-South Street on the left and of the yard on the right. Nearly orthographic: a long lens, little perspective. A few townsmen on the walk, two saddled horses at the rail, for scale.

views.title: The corner, from the crossroads
views.view: A three-quarter view from the crossroads, standing in the street south-west of the building, looking north-east: the front and the whole west side along the North-South Street, the corner, the balcony; at dusk, the sky still light, the lamps lit inside so the windows glow warm, men on the balcony and the walk.

views.title: The back and the yard (north-east)
views.view: A three-quarter view of the back and the east side from the far corner of the yard, looking south-west, in morning light: the yard with its wagon gate, the outside stair, the back door, the cellar's bulkhead hatch against the east wall, a privy, beer kegs and empties; the outside stair on the east side in the yard. The upper floor's back windows.

views.title: Plans: cellar, ground, upper (drawn from data)
Cutaway: both floors and the cellar
views.view: An architectural cutaway, a bird's-eye three-quarter view from the south-west with the roof and the front and west walls cut away and the ground cut away to show the cellar, at night with the lamps lit: the bar room full of drinkers below, the bar and back bar, the posts and girder; the dance hall above it with a dozen couples dancing and a fiddler; the cut edges show the framing clearly: balloon-framed studs, the second floor's deep joists running across onto the girder, the floorboards on them, the rafters. The rooms upstairs, the cellar's kegs. The balcony over the walk at the front on its posts. Show the open well clearly: the railed opening in the second floor over the card tables on the west side, a man leaning on its rail looking down, the dance hall's open west side along it.

views.title: Inside: from the front door
views.view: Inside at eye level, standing just inside the front door at night, looking into the bar room: the long bar with its brass rail and spittoons and the back bar's mirror, the bartender, men drinking along it; the posts down the room and the open joists of the dance floor overhead with hanging kerosene lamps; card tables with games going; the stair up; the stove; smoke in the lamplight; through the ceiling's floorboards a little light and dust from the dancing above. Above the card tables on the left the open well: a railed gallery and the open west side of the dance hall, dancers and onlookers at the rail looking down into the bar room.

views.title: Inside: from the bar
views.view: Inside at eye level at night, standing at the bar with one boot on the brass foot rail, looking back across the room toward the card tables and the front door: a poker game at a round table in the middle distance (one player with his back to the door), other tables, the faro layout, the piano, the stove, the posts; the joists of the dance floor overhead with lamps hung from them; the front windows dark with the street's lamps beyond. A shot glass and a bottle on the bar in the foreground.

views.title: Inside: the dance hall upstairs
views.view: Inside the dance hall on the upper floor at night, at eye level: a plank floor worn pale in the middle, a fiddler on his little platform, a dozen men in work clothes and their Sunday coats dancing a reel with women in plain dresses, others on benches round the walls, kerosene lamps on brackets, the doors at the front standing open onto the balcony and the night street beyond. A bare, plain room, the board walls papered or whitewashed.

views.title: Inside: looking down over the rail
views.view: Upstairs at night, standing at the turned wooden railing of the open well, looking down 13 ft into the bar room: a poker game at a round table directly below, other tables, the long bar and back bar mirror to the left, the posts and the girder, the corner door; behind the viewer the dance hall's lamps and a dancing couple at the edge of frame; another man leaning on the rail. The rail is waist high (36 in), plain turned balusters; the floor's edge shows the joists' ends and the trimmer. Vertigo: it is a real drop.
